title: NeuroVLA: A Brain-inspired Embodied Intelligence for Fluid and Fast Reflexive Robotics Control
abstract: arXiv:2601.14628v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models inherit powerful semantic representations from large language models, but carrying over their design priorities can leave the demands of physical control under-specified. Stable manipulation requires high-frequency proprioceptive feedback and persistent motor state, in addition to instruction understanding. Here we introduce Neuromorphic Vision-Language-Action (NeuroVLA), a brain-inspired architecture that couples a cortical vision-language planner to recurrent cerebellar modulation and a stateful spiking spinal controller. These components translate semantic intent into actions while incorporating high-frequency proprioceptive and force feedback, maintaining short-term motor memory, and enabling local responses to unexpected contact. In simulated and physical manipulation tasks, the cerebellar module reduces mean commanded jerk by 75.6%, and NeuroVLA achieves a 54.8% collision-recovery rate

translated_title: NeuroVLA：一种面向流畅快速反射式机器人控制的脑启发具身智能
translated_abstract: 视觉-语言-动作（VLA）模型从大语言模型中继承了强大的语义表征能力，但直接沿用其设计优先级可能会使物理控制方面的需求得不到充分满足。稳定的操作除了需要理解指令之外，还依赖高频本体感觉反馈和持续的运动状态。本文提出神经形态视觉-语言-动作模型NeuroVLA，这是一种脑启发架构，将皮层视觉-语言规划器与循环小脑调制模块和有状态的脉冲脊柱控制器相耦合。这些组件在将语义意图转化为动作的同时，融合了高频本体感觉与力反馈，维持短期运动记忆，并能够对意外接触做出局部响应。在仿真和真实物理操作任务中，小脑模块将平均指令加加速度降低了75.6%，NeuroVLA实现了54.8%的碰撞恢复率。
tldr: 提出脑启发架构NeuroVLA，通过耦合皮层视觉-语言规划器、循环小脑调制和有状态脉冲脊柱控制器，实现高频本体感觉反馈与对意外接触的反射式响应，使指令加加速度降低75.6%、碰撞恢复率达54.8%。
